rule: At least three pool hamlets carry a brook (non-vacuity of the rest of the file).
notes: This pins the pool's makeup, not a placement rule. It protects the file's other tests from passing vacuously.

rule: No lane crosses the brook without a deck whose own span reaches the crossing point.
mechanism: stage_crossings (hamletgen/frame.py:104) calls bridges() after every way and watercourse is laid. It scans every lane segment against every stream segment (bridge_carried_ways and bridge_crossed_waters, settlement/_knobs.py:589-637) and decks each crossing at the crossing point, with a span solved and grown by seat_deck (bridges.py:86-111, 197-268). Nothing adds lanes after stage_crossings.
sketch: Make the dedupe test the same as the check: skip a new deck only when an existing deck is within the existing deck's own span (or its footprint covers the crossing), not within half the new span. Otherwise draw the deck.
notes: The gap is the one-deck-per-place dedupe at bridges.py:~263: `dist < _span*0.5` of the NEW deck skips the crossing. The test measures against the EXISTING deck's span. A short channel plank within half an oblique brook deck's span but beyond its own span leaves the crossing counted as unbridged. bridge() at :~180 has the same shape (_btol).

rule: No farmstead part (garden, threshing yard, fixture, byre, shed, persimmon, bamboo stand with `of`) stands across the brook from its own house.
mechanism: Yard, gardens and shed: settlement/rolling/fit.py:_parts_fit (351) refuses the homestead when _parts_across_stream (359-380) finds the house-to-part line crossing any stream. Farm fixtures: hamletgen/homesteads/fixtures.py:613 refuses across_the_brook (786). Persimmons: fixtures.py:328 does the same.
sketch: Give draft_byres (_courtyard_byre_seat, _yard_shed_seat and its spiral) the same across_the_brook refusal and try the next seat. Move round_the_brooks before the homesteads so every bank test reads the final course. FR-013; the shared-bank rule is recorded as a GUESS in research/homesteads.
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks (stage_crossings) re-fillets the brook after every part is placed. It moves the course up to about 8-9 px toward the inside of a bend. A part whose endpoint is kept outside that sliver cannot flip banks, but this rests on the keep-out margins, not on any check.
notes: Byres (byres.py:338/360 write `of`) have no stream or bank test anywhere in byres.py. Homestead bamboo stands carry no `of`, so the test does not see them.

rule: No copse clump stands beyond 90 ft of a farmhouse (dooryard copse) or beyond 60 ft of a belt crown (against-the-belt copse).
mechanism: hamletgen/hinterland/stages.py:279 passes near=(houses, px(90)-0.1, brook). For against_the_belt it passes lee-face crowns shifted half the reach leeward with radius half (stages.py:289-290), which bounds a clump within the full reach of a crown. village_grove builds the index (stands.py:289 BankNear or Seats), and every seat path refuses outside it: the grid _seat (398), _reseat (383) and the area-goal offsets (through _seat). The windbreak-only gap fill (stands.py ~565) does the same. Unit test: tests/hamletgen/test_hinterland.py:547 test_a_bank_aware_reach_stops_at_the_brook.
notes: The 0.1 px margin covers the manifest's rounding (269 E2). set_view only repartitions clumps between clumps and clumps_offpage, and the test reads both.

rule: An entrance-seated notice board never stands more than 160 ft from the entrance anchor, nor where some household's way out does not pass within 20 ft of it.
sketch: Make routes_missed == 0 and dist(anchor) <= ENTRANCE_REACH + ANCHOR_BAND hard filters on the candidate set. Where no verge passes them, open a verge on the approach inside the handover band (the connector is every departure's way). Give stage_notice's re-seat the same filters. FR-015 / SC-011; research/urban-features.html (the kosatsu at the village entrance, broadside to the way out).
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/frame.py:stage_notice re-seats a board that falls outside the view. It uses the same 'fewest missed' ranking and a band relative to the nearest seat.
notes: siting.py:451-453 keeps the seats with the FEWEST missed departures (min, not zero). The handover band (530) is relative to the nearest surviving seat (_hnear + 20 ft), not absolute. So a map whose best seat misses a household, or stands far off, still ships. departure_routes also drops houses beyond 150 ft of a lane.

rule: No vertex of the brook's drawn course turns it by more than 100 degrees.
mechanism: brook_skirt returns unfold(...) (brook.py:342-344). unfold (107-127) deletes every vertex turning more than BROOK_MAX_TURN_DEG and repeats until none does. That covers the course below the tap. round_the_brooks (frame.py:56-67) then only fillets corners, which splits a turn into smaller ones.
sketch: In feed_brook, refuse an approach bearing (the 15-swing loop) whose entry into the sluice plus the first skirt leg turns more than the limit, and move on to the next swing. Or run unfold over the whole assembled course while holding the tap vertex. GM 2026-08-26 / FR-017.
later_stage_risk: round_the_brooks holds the tap vertex unrounded (hold=taps), so a sharp turn at the sluice survives it.
notes: Unguarded: the approach legs (the up, mid and three wobble points, brook.py:372-380) and the joint approach -> sluice -> first skirt point. The approach bearing may swing up to 70 degrees off the fall, and the last wobble leg is about 30 px with up to 16 px of lateral jitter.

rule: On a brook map, some internal lane always comes within 60 ft of the paddy or its dry hem.
mechanism: The last word of stage_web (web.py). It returns 'joined' when a lane end is within BUND_REACH_FT of the paddy with no water between. Otherwise it runs the nearest end onto the bund (over the water), or draws a branch path from the nearest lane sample (bund.py:181-236).
sketch: Make the 'none: ...' outcome impossible. Let the branch cross water at a ford or ditch (stage_crossings decks it), as the run-on already does. Failing that, feed the stranded field into the driver's re-roll like unreached_houses. FR-012 / SC-008; research/fields/290 (the path never ends short of the bund).
notes: When every straight way from the lanes to the paddy crosses water, the marsh or a steading, the function returns 'none: ...' and the map ships with no way to the field. meta.field_path records it, but nothing refuses it.

rule: No stretch of brook within 80 ft of the view's edge runs level along that edge (within 4 ft) for more than 150 ft.
sketch: The frame is decided later (stage_frame, crop_to_content with brook_beside_the_field as extra), so hold the course to the same box the reservation predicts. Break at the first station the box binds, not only after half the stations. Bend or turn any exit leg that runs parallel to, and within 80 ft of, a box edge. Or assert it in stage_frame and widen the crop. GM 2026-08-26 (Sawada: 'makes it look like a mistake').
later_stage_risk: stage_frame's crop_to_content decides the view the test measures against, after the brook is drawn.
notes: brook.py:254 breaks off the frame only when i > steps//2 and the frame-box binds. The first half of the stations can still be laid flat against the box. The exit legs (278-287) are straight runs on a heading blended to the fall, and nothing tests them against the eventual view. The box is the field's bounds plus 44 px, not the view.

rule: No farmhouse corner stands within the brook's half-width plus 5 ft of its course.
mechanism: At seat time _parts_fit (fit.py:351) refuses a homestead whose house rect touches a stream at half-width + 5 px (_rect_on_stream 249-266, rect_touches_stream). That is the test's own bar.
sketch: Round the brook before the homesteads are seated (at the water stage, since every way is routed after the houses anyway), so the seat test reads the final course. Or re-check the house rects against the rounded course in round_the_brooks and refuse the rounding radius locally. FR-013.
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks (stage_crossings) fillets the brook after the houses are seated. The curve lies inside the bend, up to about d*cos(interior/2)/2 (about 8-9 px at the 100-degree limit) toward a house on the inside, which is enough to bring a corner within the bar.
notes: The test builds axis-aligned corners from h.w/h.h. The placer tests the rect's own corners (_rect_corners), which may be rotated by _house_rot, so the two can disagree on a raked house.

rule: No lane record is an empty husk, no lane's end runs on alongside another way, no lane crosses the brook an even number of times (2+), and no crossing stands more than 45 ft from a ford.
owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/web.py:stage_web (its closing passes; see notes for each clause's owner)
mechanism: Fords: track.py:275-278 gaps the brook at the fords (stream_segs, checks.py:34-50) and tolls entry to its band (route.py set_crossing/_new_crossing), so every router and string-pull that receives stream_segs can cross only in a 30 px gap. Husks: web.py drops lanes under 2 points or 1 ft after cut_past_the_junction.
sketch: Refuse the even-crossing fallback in _join_orphan_ways (leave the orphan to the straggler pass or the re-roll). Make the doubled-tail sweep ask every neighbor regardless of width and run it after the last lane rewrite. Give meet_end_to_end and every late rewrite a water/ford test (the stream_segs list). Check all four as an invariant at the end of stage_web. FR-011; settlement-reviews of Kashikawa and Mizuguchi.
later_stage_risk: meet_end_to_end (joints.py:297), center_lane_ends, cut_at_tail's snap and a_way_onto_the_bund's run-on rewrite lanes after the routed passes, and none of them reads stream_segs. round_the_brooks moves the course after the fords were recorded.
notes: Even crossings: sweeps.py:305-311 keeps an even-crossing link as a FALLBACK when nothing else links the orphan, and no pass checks crossing parity per lane. Doubled tails: _sweep_doubled_tails (sweeps.py:942) skips spur lanes and never cuts along a NARROWER lane, but the test asks every pair. Eight passes follow it (center_lane_ends, cut_the_overruns, cut_past_the_junction, split_at_crossings, tidy_lane_ends, meet_end_to_end, a_way_onto_the_bund, then square_crossings).

rule: The notice board's drawn caption never lies on a farmhouse roof or within 2 ft of a lane's tread.
mechanism: place() returns the first candidate with cost 0 (placer.py:195-208). Every built footprint is an obstacle at CLEAR_EM*size (4 ft), and every lane is a way at half-width + WAY_NOTCH (2 ft) (labels/obstacles.py cost). So a cost-0 seat satisfies the test. The siter ranks board seats by board_caption_level, which calls the same place() (siting.py:118-140).
sketch: Treat a board seat whose caption level is 0 as refused in place_kosatsuba and in the stage_notice re-seat, and let the label phase seat the caption against the index the siter probed with. Or re-site the board in the label phase when place() returns cost > 0.
later_stage_risk: stage_labels seats the caption against the label-phase obstacle index, which also holds captions placed earlier in the queue. It can differ from the index board_caption_level probed at siting.
notes: place() never refuses. When every candidate has cost > 0 it draws the cheapest, which may be on a roof or a lane (placer.py:209-214). The siter keeps a board even when the best level is 0.

rule: The board caption never stands nearer another built footprint than its own board.
sketch: Add a cost term (or a hard refusal for point subjects) when another obstacle's gap to the block is at or below the block's gap to its own subject, so a caption that names a neighbor is never cost-0. The cartographic standard's proximity principle (research/presentation, 'Where does a caption sit').
later_stage_risk: The label phase's index differs from the siter's probe (see the previous test).
notes: At cost 0 the caption is at least 4 ft from other obstacles, and at ring 0 it is 4 ft from its own board: a tie is allowed (the test is strict). At ring > 0 the caption is farther from its board while the others need only 4 ft, so a neighbor can be nearer. Nothing compares the two distances.

rule: No household's way out (through the lanes and along the connector) crosses the brook more than once.
sketch: Refuse the over-and-back link where it is made (the _join_orphan_ways fallback). After _link_home_bank, and again after the last lane pass, recompute departure_routes and treat a household with 2+ crossings as unreached, so the driver's re-roll or the straggler pass owns it. Settlement-review of Mizuguchi (feature 261).
later_stage_risk: Passes after _link_home_bank (straighten_joints, _sweep_doubled_tails, cut_the_overruns, tidy_lane_ends' drops, split_at_crossings, meet_end_to_end) change the graph departure_routes walks. stage_crossings squares crossings.
notes: _link_home_bank (sweeps.py:338-384) repairs excursions only where _serve_stragglers succeeds in laying a home-bank way. When it lays nothing the excursion ships. It runs once and is not re-checked.

rule: No lane's first or last leg is 12 ft or shorter and turns back 90 degrees or more.
sketch: Make hook removal the invariant of the lane commit (commit_lane / reink_lane refuse to write a hooked lane). Or run _one_hook as the very last lane pass, after stage_crossings' squaring too. Where unhooked cannot keep the end on its ways, cut at the vertex before and let the touch pass re-join it. GM 2026-09-26.
later_stage_risk: center_lane_ends, cut_the_overruns, cut_past_the_junction, split_at_crossings, tidy_lane_ends, meet_end_to_end, a_way_onto_the_bund (all after straighten_joints in stage_web), and square_crossings in stage_crossings.
notes: straighten_joints (joints.py:163-190) removes a hook only when unhooked() returns a cut (140-156) and keeps_the_web plus commit_lane accept it. Otherwise the hook stays. Eight later rewrites can make new short last legs.

rule: No lane crosses a drawn channel more than 10 degrees off square.
mechanism: stage_crossings (frame.py:95-103) runs square_crossings for every drawn channel against every lane. It replaces an off-square crossing with a leg along the channel's normal (checks.py:350-381).
sketch: Where the crossing segment is too short, split the segment or move the adjoining vertex so the square leg fits, instead of leaving it. Handle every crossing on a segment, not just the first. Re-square against all waters until a pass changes nothing. Research ways/030 (a plank crosses its ditch square).
later_stage_risk: Squaring against one water can make a lane oblique to another nearby (the head race beside the brook at the intake). Nothing re-checks the earlier water.
notes: checks.py:376 leaves a crossing as drawn when it lies within `half` of either end of its segment, and `break` (379) squares only the first crossing per segment. The routers hold ditches only to the 42-degree shallow_crossing bound.

rule: The notice board's caption is never drawn at an angle other than the board's own, modulo 180 degrees.
mechanism: boards.py:_draw_board_caption passes Subject('point', ..., angle=rot) with the board's own rot, the same rot kosatsuba() records. _point_cands sets every candidate's angle to upright(subject.angle) (placer.py:90-110), so every seat, fallback included, is at the board's angle mod 180. Unit test: tests/settlement/test_finish.py:130 test_label_carries_the_subjects_own_angle_for_lines_and_boxes_alike.
notes: Rounding: the record's rot is rounded to 0.1 degrees against the test's 0.5 tolerance.

rule: No three woodland parcels stand in a ruled line (the third off the line through two others by less than 20% of their span).
sketch: Re-ask in_a_ruled_line on the final seat, after the jitter and size roll (refuse the jitter, as _ok does), and on the point the record will carry. Or make the record's x,y the seat center the rule was asked of. Settlement-reviews of 2026-08-18 and of Inashiro (feature 261).
later_stage_risk: settlement/land/cover.py:commons records x,y as the vertex mean of the irregular ring, not the seat.
notes: seat_off_the_row (parcels.py:176-181, called at 463) checks the lattice seat. The seat is then jittered by up to half a step and re-tested only by _ok (about 480-510), never by in_a_ruled_line. The drawn ring's recorded centroid is a third point. The test reads the recorded x,y.

rule: No copse clump's center stands inside any marsh polygon.
mechanism: For role == 'copse', every marsh polygon of 3+ points is added to GroveBlocks' dikes (stands.py ~269). GroveBlocks.hard (grove_blocks.py:96-99) refuses a point inside it, and hard() is asked on every copse seat path: _seat (398) and _reseat (381). The gap fill is windbreak-only.
notes: The placer tests unrounded seats and the record rounds to 0.1 px, so a seat within 0.05 px of a marsh edge could read inside. No marsh is drawn after stage_windbreak. research/vegetation.html (woody cover on the dry ground above the marsh).

rule: The board caption never lies on a tree crown unless meta.kosatsuba_caption_level records that no seat offered a clear caption (level 1).
sketch: Give the canopy to the label-phase placer as an obstacle (weighted below roofs) for the board's caption, so the drawn seat is the one ranked clear. Record kosatsuba_caption_level from the DRAWN caption in _draw_board_caption rather than from the siter's probe.
later_stage_risk: stage_labels re-seats the caption against a different index (the other captions), and place() does not weigh the canopy at all.
notes: The siter ranks seats by board_caption_level (siting.py:118-140, level 2 = clear of crowns) and records the level of ITS probe (siting.py:555; frame.py:352). The caption actually drawn is seated later by place() with no canopy term, so a probe-clear seat can be drawn on a crown while meta says 2, or the other way round.

rule: No dooryard copse clump lacks a farmhouse within 90 ft whose line to it crosses no reach of the brook.
mechanism: stages.py:279 passes the brook segments as barriers. BankNear.too_near (stands.py:20-36) admits a clump only when some house within reach has an uncrossed line to it, and every copse seat path asks it (398, 383). Unit test: tests/hamletgen/test_hinterland.py:547.
sketch: Harden by rounding the brook before the woods are placed (the same move as for the houses), so the barrier is the drawn course.
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks fillets the course afterward. A line that crossed no old reach can cross the fillet only if an endpoint lies in the sliver between the corner and the curve (at most about 9 px deep). Clumps are kept half-width + crown radius (about 17 ft or more) off the stream by GroveBlocks.water, and house centers are further. So it holds by margin, not by a check.
notes: This is the bank half of the copse rule. The reach half is the test above.

rule: No straight run of the brook (every vertex within 3.1 ft of the chord) covers more than 40% of its in-view length (when that length is 300 ft or more).
sketch: Measure the straightest run of the course inside the predicted frame box before returning. Where it exceeds 40%, add bends (exit_bend on the offending legs, or more lateral wander where the crop floor does not bind) until it does not. Settlement-review of Sawada (round 0ae309f0); GM 2026-08-26 on ruled courses.
later_stage_risk: stage_frame decides the view that 'on the page' is measured in. round_the_brooks only rounds corners.
notes: The wander, the corner cut and exit_bend (brook.py:278-287) make straight runs less likely, and brook.py:233-248 records that where the crop's floor binds, the walk cannot loosen a ruled run. Nothing measures the run.

rule: No per-household grain plot (dry_plots[].homestead, meta.homestead_fields) is ever laid by a house.
mechanism: No code path in l7r/ writes `homestead` on a dry plot or meta.homestead_fields (grep for homestead_fields, '"homestead": True' and 'homestead=True' returns nothing). The map cannot carry one.
notes: This is a regression guard against re-adding a retired form (the GM, 2026-09-28; research/homesteads.html and research/fields.html). It could move to a static test of the engine rather than a rolled map.

rule: No windbreak clump seated inside a toe or waterside marsh is drawn as anything but alder, and the grove's recorded alder count equals the number of its on-page clumps in the marsh.
mechanism: The drawing is by construction: stands.py:638-641 draws every seated clump inside a toe or waterside marsh with mix='alder' and counts it.
sketch: Recount `alder` over the on-page clumps when set_view partitions them (core.py:_partition_grove_clumps), or record alder and alder_offpage separately. Test the rounded record points the same way. research/vegetation.html (the marsh margin: alder or willow, never pine).
later_stage_risk: settlement/core.py:_partition_grove_clumps (from set_view in stage_frame) moves clumps between clumps and clumps_offpage after `alder` was counted over every seated clump.
notes: The count covers all `seated` (on and off page), while the test counts only g['clumps'] (on page after the partition). An off-page wet clump makes them differ. The unrounded seat and the rounded record can also disagree at a marsh edge.

rule: No brook segment of 10 ft or longer (other than the two tap-run segments) lies within 1.6 degrees of a screen axis.
mechanism: _off_the_axes (brook.py:130-160) nudges any segment within eps of an axis. It is applied to the skirt with hold=1 (brook.py:343) and to the approach legs (380).
sketch: Apply _off_the_axes AFTER unfold and iterate the pair until both hold. Include the approach's last leg into the sluice while holding the sluice point (nudge the leg's start). GM 2026-08-26.
later_stage_risk: round_the_brooks keeps each leg's own bearing for its straight remainder, and its fillet chords are mostly under the 10 ft exemption. A leg cut short by fillets on both ends stays on its old bearing, so no new axis segments are made except by the vertex drops above.
notes: Unguarded: (1) unfold runs AFTER _off_the_axes in brook_skirt (342-343), so deleting a folded vertex makes a new segment that is never re-checked. (2) The approach's _off_the_axes list is [up, mid, w1, w2, w3] without the sluice, so the segment w3 -> sluice (which the test does not exempt) is never checked.

rule: No lane crosses the brook more than 10 degrees off square.
mechanism: stage_crossings rounds the brook first (frame.py:89), then squares every lane against every stream (95-103). square_crossings drops interior vertices within `half` of the brook (the elbow in the water) and replaces an off-square crossing with a leg along the brook's normal (checks.py:350-381). The ford gap already limits a routed crossing to about 40 degrees off square.
sketch: As for the channels: split or extend a segment too short to hold the square leg, square every crossing on a segment, and iterate over streams and channels together until nothing changes. Or square at the router by forcing the path through the two ford landings (ford_crossing) that the connector already uses. Settlement-review of Kashikawa (round 03cf6a84).
later_stage_risk: The channel squaring pass runs after the stream pass on the same lanes (frame.py:96-97). At the intake, where the head race leaves the brook, squaring a lane to the race can leave its brook crossing oblique.
notes: checks.py:376 skips a crossing within `half` of either end of the crossing segment (the lane's end or the dropped-vertex neighbor), and `break` squares only the first crossing per segment.

rule: No internal lane end reaches nothing (way, house, bund or steading) except the way its own far end stands on.
sketch: Have _trim_to_service ask end_serves with the test's segment set (the other lanes minus those within _TOUCH_GAP of the lane's own far end), and trim or drop by it. Run it after the last end-moving pass (meet_end_to_end, a_way_onto_the_bund). Keep a lane that is some house's only way by carrying it on to the house rather than exempting it. Settlement-review of Mizuguchi (round 176042d3).
later_stage_risk: meet_end_to_end and a_way_onto_the_bund move ends after tidy_lane_ends. stage_crossings' squaring moves vertices.
notes: tidy_lane_ends trims against EVERY other lane, including the one the lane left. So a short lane whose free end is still within 60 ft of its own origin way counts as served. A trim that would fall under _WEB_MIN_FT is left whole when the lane is some house's `keep`.

rule: departure_routes does not route a house from a lane sample beyond `reach`.
notes: This is a unit test on a constructed manifest of the route-walking helper (settlement/structures/fixtures/_helpers.py:departure_routes), which the board siter and _link_home_bank use as a measure. It does not test a placer.

rule: No paddy bund edge may stand inside a supply canal's or delivery ditch's drawn stroke (halfw + BANK_MARGIN).
owner: l7r/diagram/waterfields/seams/close.py:close_seams (last to reshape rings; the carve half is waterfields/carve.py:_carve_plots)
mechanism: The CARVE refuses by the gate's own predicate: carve.py:_clear_supply pushes every corner onto the bank (need = halfw + BANK_MARGIN*g) and carve.py:_quad_in_supply/_edge_in_supply walk each edge at 3 px and DROP a quad still inside (threshold halfw + BANK_MARGIN*g - 0.5, stricter than the gate's BANK_MARGIN - 0.15); _hem_pass applies the same. close_seams plants only `field - covered - _water(channels, g)` (seams/pockets.py:_water, per-segment buffers at taper-at-segment-head + BANK_MARGIN*g, discs at bends), and seams/plots.py:_trade refuses a new wall that intersects `water`.
sketch: Close the unguarded producers in close_seams: _shed_necks (grows a basin by tail.buffer(0.05) with no water test), _absorb (union + simplify(0.05)), _repair_crossing_rings (buffer(0) part) - run the carve's _quad_in_supply on every ring a seam-pass step rewrites and refuse/revert the step. Also _water buffers a segment at its HEAD width only; a widening stroke (w_tail > w) is under-covered - buffer at max(w_i, w_i+1). GM rule 2026-08-15 (bunds abut the water's edge).
later_stage_risk: close_seams (_shed_necks, _absorb simplify, _repair_crossing_rings) and _comb_toe_and_hem's hem_to_bank run after the carve's guarantee.
notes: Placer margin at g=2 is ~0.9 px stricter than the gate, which is why it holds in practice; the seam pass guards by geometric subtraction, not by the gate predicate.

rule: No plot-ring edge may run across the drain collector (both ends within half the stroke of its centerline).
mechanism: The carve hems onto the drain BANK by construction (frame.py:_drain_bank via carve.py:_bnd/_bank_chord; _hem_pass builds hem quads parallel to the drain chord). comb.py:_comb_toe_and_hem then runs banks.py:hem_to_bank on every ring, lifting any vertex inside the stroke or past the centerline up-fall onto the bank. close_seams plants only outside _water (drain included).
sketch: Make the terminal invariant terminal: hem_to_bank exempts vertices where `lean < 0.2` (drain running with the fall) and `past` (beyond the drain's ends), and it runs BEFORE close_seams, whose welds/trades/necks can re-shape rings. Re-run the drain-bank clearance on rings close_seams rewrites (refuse the step) or move hem_to_bank's check to the end of close_seams. GM 2026-08-08 (hem bunds run with the ditch).
later_stage_risk: close_seams (_absorb, _shed_necks, _repair_crossing_rings) after the toe pass.

rule: No azemame bead may sit on water paint (inside any field ditch, channel stroke, or the pond).
mechanism: waterfields/carve.py:_bund_beans drops beads buried by later plots and by the net's own channel strokes (wet(), half-width + tol); settlement/fields/comb.py:_comb_drop_drowned_beads then re-splits every run against the source pond, field ponds, and every field_ditch and channel ALREADY in M (same seg_dist < half test as the gate).
sketch: The drop reads M at one moment; water recorded after it is never tested: `_comb_source_channel` (a pond-fed field's bowed hairline into the paddy, w 2.5) is appended AFTER the drop in draw_comb_field, and hamletgen/sink.py:drain_run (stage_sink) later still. Run the drop at finish over the final water registry (or have every channel recorder re-filter beads), keeping bead_runs so the two-bead rule survives.
later_stage_risk: settlement/fields/comb.py:_comb_source_channel (same draw_comb_field call, after the drop); hamletgen/sink.py:drain_run; any later M['channels'] append.
notes: The gate's pond is M['pond']; a sink tameike is sited clear of the envelope (sink.py:pond_setback), so it cannot bury a bead.

rule: Self-test of the test's own bead-segment derivation on constructed rings.
notes: Tests the test helper _bead_segments, not a placer.

rule: No beaded bund segment may show a single bead (GM 2026-09-14: at least two glyphs).
mechanism: carve.py:bead_runs splits a bead line at every rejected bead and keeps only parts of MIN_BEADS_PER_RUN (2) or more; _bund_beans lays each edge's line (nd==2 -> 3 so a short edge carries two, step < 1.34*spacing so consecutive beads stay within the gate's 1.5-spacing join) and filters through bead_runs; the draw-site drop (settlement/fields/comb.py:_comb_drop_drowned_beads) re-splits through bead_runs too. Beads are laid after close_seams on the final rings, so they sit on recorded ring edges.
later_stage_risk: Any future bead drop that does not go through bead_runs (e.g. the fix for the previous row) must use it.
notes: Unit tests of bead_runs are the placer-level proof (feature 247).

rule: Neighboring dry plots of one tract may not differ by more than 2x the in-tract turn; neighbors across a tract seam must differ by more than ~6 deg.
mechanism: Within a tract: carve.py:_dry_fields sets theta = tract heading + U(-TRACT_PLOT_TURN_RAD, +TRACT_PLOT_TURN_RAD), so any two plots of a tract differ by <= 0.10 rad (the gate's bar). Seams between CONSECUTIVE tracts of one band: furrows.py:tract_ways forces furrow_turn(heading, prev) >= TRACT_SEAM_MIN_RAD (0.35), leaving >= 0.25 after per-plot jitter.
sketch: Seams are forced only against the previous tract in sequence. Unguarded: the fork-triangle band (_comb_dry_and_beans' second _dry_fields call, tract0 offset) against first-band tracts it abuts, and non-consecutive tracts that end up spatially adjacent. Force a seam against every tract whose plots neighbor the new one (spatial adjacency, as the gate reads it). Research fields/180.
later_stage_risk: fan_toe_hem and _comb_draw_hem only remove plots, which cannot create a new within-tract split but can bring the second band beside the first.

rule: Self-test of the tract judge on a constructed manifest.
notes: Tests the test helper _tract_pairs.

rule: A polder dike's widest stretch must be at least 1.4x its narrowest (never a uniform-width band).
sketch: Width is wlo + (whi-wlo)*clamp(0.5 + three seeded sines) + U(-3,3); with the default (14, 40) the ratio is usually well past 1.4, but nothing bounds it (phases can flatten the sum). After w_seen is built, if max/min < DIKE_IRREGULARITY, stretch the profile about its mean (deterministic, no new draw) until it holds. Research: fish-scale polder dike (archetypes.html).
notes: The 1.4 lives only in the test; the placer should own the constant.

rule: No house, farm shed, byre or threshing yard may stand (by its center) inside the dike's keep-out.
mechanism: dikes.py:~201-205 builds the keep-out with keepout_ring (contains every band vertex, tests/settlement/test_keepouts.py), records it as `keepout` AND appends it to self.block_polys, in stage 2 before any homestead. Bundles (house/yard/shed) are refused by hamletgen/homesteads/boundary.py:site_boundary, which unions block_polys into the containment outline asked by settlement/rolling/fit.py:_site_blocks_rect at nine points; byres, yards and gardens refuse a center in block_polys via _in_blocked (shrines_wells/byres.py:160, homestead_parts/yards.py:437).
later_stage_risk: Dike-top houses are exempt by design (on_dike); none on hamlets.

rule: No watercourse may cross the dike crest except within 60 px of a recorded gap (sluice or outfall).
mechanism: hamletgen/water/polder.py:dike_gaps_at_channels adds a gap wherever a NET channel segment crosses the inner ring (envelope), and perimeter_dike cuts the band there.
sketch: Only net['channels'] crossing the INNER ring are gapped: M['channels'] (the reservoir inlet hairline, stage_sink's drain_run) and any course running along the crest without crossing the inner ring get no gap. Compute gaps from every recorded course against the crest band after the water is final, or make later channel routers treat the dike band as a keep-out except at its gaps.
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/sink.py:stage_sink/drain_run and draw_comb_field's _comb_source_channel add channels outside the gap computation.

rule: A waterward reed strip must reach the map's view edge on its flank, never stop inside the frame.
sketch: The strip's outer edge is the dike's extreme minus WATERWARD_DEPTH (280 px, consts.py), a constant measured to outlast every crop seen so far; the view is decided later by the crop, which ignores the strip. Either clamp the crop so it never extends past a waterward strip's outer edge, or extend the strip to the final view after cropping. GM 2026-08-28 / feature 150 T55.
later_stage_risk: The crop (crop_to_content / the frame stage) decides meta.view after the strip is laid.

rule: Every ditched paddy field must have a base floor drawn under its plots.
mechanism: draw_comb_field calls comb_base_fill unconditionally before the plots; it draws and records M['comb_floors'][name] whenever the net has any plot vertex (returns early only with no plots, in which case the field has no rings).

rule: The fan's floor outline may not overhang the flat-extended collector line by more than 16 px down-fall.
mechanism: _comb_floor_and_winding pulls every envelope vertex whose banks.py:floor_overhang (the gate's own predicate) exceeds 0.5 px back up-fall onto the line, then dedup_ring (removes vertices only).
later_stage_risk: The trim is against raw dpts; round_channel_joints can reshape the recorded drain at a record seam and the manifest rounds to 0.1 px - both far under the 16 px tolerance.

rule: Each flank of the fork must have supply ditch reach of at least max(80 ft, 30% of that flank's planted extent).
sketch: It holds by the skeleton's proportions (canal A at down-42 deg, canal B at down+58 deg, offtakes along both) but nothing measures it; BROOK_FAN_TRIM shortens one canal. Add a both-flanks predicate to the fit's legality score (beside tail_dangles / net_bends_acutely) so an aspect/size that leaves a flank uncommanded is illegal, or constrain canal lengths per flank. GM 2026-08-16.
later_stage_risk: fit_field keeps the closest-on-acreage fan even when no aspect is legal.

rule: No paddy basin ring (as recorded) may have an interior angle under 15 deg.
mechanism: Every seam-pass producer refuses needles: _plant's output judged raw+dedup at _TOE_MIN_APEX 25 (close.py:~172), _visible_parts raw+dedup at 25, _absorb via _weld_apex (raw at 15, dedup at 18; fallback only >= 16), seams/plots.py:_trade via _is_a_needle (raw+dedup at 15), _shed_necks and _repair_crossing_rings at _GATE_MIN_APEX. The toe pass (comb.py:_comb_toe_and_hem) drops rings pointed at 25 deg.
sketch: The toe pass judges only dedup_ring(r, 1.0); a carved ring that no seam step touches is never judged on the RAW ring the gate reads (a sub-pixel edge can hide a raw apex). Add a terminal sweep at the end of close_seams (after _repair_crossing_rings) that sends any plot pointed on either reading to _absorb as a scrap. GM realism ruling 2026-08-17.

rule: No plot painted with the flooded tint may be a needle (raw ring under 15 deg).
mechanism: close_seams re-judges every FLOODED plot's final ring and demotes it to green when pointed_ring(dedup_ring(p,1.0), 25), tapers_to_a_point, low solidity, at the outfall, aspect, rectangularity or size fail; the promotion of one plot when none survives uses the same `_wrong` predicate.
sketch: The re-judge reads the DEDUPED ring while the gate now reads the raw ring; add pointed_ring(raw, 25) to `_wrong` (the carve's own comment says both rings are needed).
notes: Comments in close.py say the gate reads dedup_ring; the test reads rings[best] raw - the two drifted.

rule: No basin may be smaller than _GATE_MIN_AREA (0.20) of the fan's design cell.
mechanism: comb.py:_comb_toe_and_hem drops rings under _TOE_MIN_AREA (0.25); close_seams sends planted part-tiles under _TOE_MIN_AREA to scraps, _visible_parts drops cut plots under it, seams/plots.py:_trade refuses any ring under `floor` = _GATE_MIN_AREA*cell; _absorb only grows.
sketch: _shed_necks shrinks the giving basin (body = largest part after the tail) with no area test, and _repair_crossing_rings keeps the largest part of a buffer(0) with no area test. Add the _GATE_MIN_AREA floor to both (refuse the trade / send the remainder to _absorb). GM 2026-08-17 ('a few very small triangles').

rule: The recorded plot rings may not over-count the fan's area by 4% or more (overlap stays marginal).
mechanism: close_seams opens with _visible_parts (close.py:359-425), which cuts every plot to the part no later plot covers (a partition up to 1 px^2); everything after plants from `field.difference(covered)` or trades ground conservatively (_trade: `was.difference(now)` handed over; _shed_necks: tail moved), so overlap is bounded by the 0.02-0.05 px buffers/simplify tolerances.
notes: The test docstring still describes the pre-230 lapping stack; the partition makes the ceiling near-vacuous.

rule: No plot ring may carry more than one bund step (jog) - no staircase walls.
sketch: _absorb PREFERS a weld that adds no jog but falls back to the least-jogged weld (`_jogged` branch), and _unjog REPAIRS steps but refuses a trade that would break another rule, leaving the step. Nothing refuses a ring with >1 step. Make >1 step a refusal in _absorb (treat a jog-adding weld like a needle: try _open_to / the next host) and add a terminal check after _unjog that sends a remaining staircase to the scrap path. GM 2026-08-18 on Inashiro.
later_stage_risk: _shed_necks and _repair_crossing_rings run after _unjog and are not jog-aware.
notes: Single steps are ledgered as allowed; the rule is >1.

rule: No recorded plot ring (rounded to 0.1 px) may cross itself.
mechanism: close_seams ends with _repair_crossing_rings(plots, rounded=True) (close.py:521-547): every ring is judged as the manifest rounds it, a crossing ring is replaced by its largest valid buffer(0) part if that part is valid when rounded and not a needle, and any ring still invalid is DROPPED. Nothing after it changes ring geometry (the tint pass only recolors).

rule: No basin ring on any shipped hamlet (every field with plot rings, polders included) may taper under 15 deg.
mechanism: Comb fans: as for test_no_basin_tapers_to_a_point (every seam-pass producer refuses needles on raw and deduped rings).
sketch: Two holes: (1) carved comb rings untouched by the seam pass are judged only on the deduped ring (toe pass); (2) polder parcels (build_polder/_polder_parcels, clean_polder_parcels, hem_to_bank) have no apex guard at all. Add the raw+dedup apex refusal as a terminal pass in both engines.
later_stage_risk: polder.py:_polder_close runs hem_to_bank, which can sharpen an apex, after the parcels are cut.

rule: The manifest must declare meta.down_deg (non-vacuity for the flow rules).
notes: A declaration check, not a placement rule.

rule: Every M['channels'] course's net displacement must run down the fall by at least 20% of its length.
owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/sink.py:stage_sink (the last router that adds channels)
mechanism: The head-race hairline follows comb.py:_comb_skeleton's race at plan.head_deg = down_deg -/+ OFFTAKE_DEG (35), so along/L = cos 35 = 0.82 by construction. A drainage-pond run ends at the pond, seated `back` > 0 down-fall (sink.py:pond_seat/pond_setback) with bounded sway.
sketch: stage_sink holds only weaker bars than the rule: brook_join needs a descent of 20 px over a reach up to 420 (0.05, not 0.2), the off-map route needs descent > 0, and when no route is clean it takes the least-bad one. Put the rule's 0.2 fraction into brook_join's and the off-map route's refusals. The head-race start snap (<= 30 px onto a stream) in _comb_source_channel is also untested against the fraction.

rule: A drain collector's outfall may not sit more than 1 px uphill of its head.
mechanism: _comb_drain fits f = a + b*u with b clamped to >= 0.06 and sorts by u, so the line falls toward the outfall (appended at hi_u with no jitter).
sketch: Every interior vertex, including the HEAD at lo_u, gets U(-6, 6) of fall jitter, so the outfall is only b*(hi_u - lo_u) below the head's line; a span under ~100 px lets the jitter put the head below the outfall. Clamp the head's jitter to <= b*span - 1 (or no jitter on the head), which makes it by construction.
later_stage_risk: round_channel_joints can reshape a seam arc; ends are preserved.

rule: The runoff's continuation (sink pond, drain run, or any brook near the outfall) must lie/run downhill of the outfall.
mechanism: Pond: sink.py:pond_seat returns back >= pry + 58 down-fall, and a clamped/obstructed seat falls back to off-map. Brook join: brook_join refuses any candidate with descent < BROOK_JOIN_DESCENT (20). Off-map: refuses descent <= 0.
sketch: The off-map loop's least-bad fallback (sink.py ~475) ships a route that failed the descent test; refuse instead (e.g. extend the search or re-seat). The test also judges ANY stream within 60 px of the outfall, including the feed brook routed past the fan by brook_skirt, which no sink logic governs - the brook's direction near the outfall should be asserted by brook_skirt.

rule: No stream's interior vertex may lie inside a field outline.
mechanism: feed_brook tries bearings until the approach chords do not cross the envelope; brook_skirt builds the course below the tap in the fall frame holding v outside every cultivated ring's profile plus a skirt.
sketch: The approach is tested on its chord BEFORE the +-16 px wobble and _off_the_axes nudges are applied; the tap run (BROOK_TAP_RUN) is deliberately not floored ('crop at the fan's head yields'); unfold() and round_the_brooks move points after the floor. Re-test the final course against the envelope and refuse/re-route.
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks (fillets the course later).

rule: A stream end declared off-map must lie off the canvas; one declared to a pond must lie on it.
sketch: The brook's frm=offmap start is a fixed `run` = 420 px from the sluice on a bearing up to 70 deg off upslope, while the sluice is placed 0.36*min(W,H) from the center (fit.py:head_sluice); nothing checks the start is past the canvas edge. Derive the run from the distance to the canvas edge along the bearing (as stage_sink already does for the off-map drain).
notes: If meta W/H are rewritten to a cropped canvas later, that is what currently makes it hold; not verified here.

rule: Every paddy field must have a channel declared to it or a field ditch naming it.
mechanism: _comb_skeleton always appends the head race; draw_comb_field unconditionally records every net channel as a field_ditch with field=name (_comb_record_ditches), and _comb_source_channel adds a channel to={'kind':'field','name':name} for non-cascade sources.

rule: Both ends of every polder lateral must land within 13 px of the main or the drain.
mechanism: _polder_channels snaps each interior lateral's tips onto the feeder and drain centerlines (`_onto`, lat_xy[0]/lat_xy[-1]); the toe laterals are the ring's own sides, sharing corner vertices with feeder and drain; banks.py:round_channel_joints moves a seam's end onto the shared arc for both records.
later_stage_risk: stage_polder moves only the feeder's inlet stub end.

rule: No channel or field ditch may cross a stream except at its own end (a confluence).
mechanism: brook_skirt keeps the brook outside every cultivated ring plus a skirt, so it cannot meet in-field ditches; the head race and the brook-join drain run end ON the brook (confluences).
sketch: No placer asks the crossing question: ditches that run outside the envelope (delivery tails, the collector's ends) and stage_sink's off-map drain run are never tested against the brook. Add a stream-crossing refusal to stage_sink's route search and to brook_skirt's profile (the ditch stretches outside the crop).
later_stage_risk: round_the_brooks reshapes the course after routing.

rule: A channel declaring a stream end must reach within 13 px of that stream's bed.
owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks (the last stage that moves the bed)
mechanism: The intake starts on the brook's tap vertex (settlement/fields/comb.py:_comb_source_channel snaps within 30 px; the hamlet's brook passes through the sluice), and round_the_brooks HOLDS the tap vertices. brook_join places the drain run's end on the brook's centerline.
sketch: The drain run's confluence (sink.py:brook_join) is not held by round_the_brooks, so a join near a brook vertex can be left off the filleted course; hold confluences too (or re-snap the run's end after rounding). The intake snap only fires within 30 px.
later_stage_risk: hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks.

rule: No watercourse bed may be painted above the topmost sheen (water composites as one surface).
mechanism: finish.py:~720-745 emits every water entry's bed inside one opacity group, then every sheen in a later group, recording bedz/sheenz from the same counter, so every sheenz > every bedz.
notes: A paint-order property, fixed by the flush's structure.

rule: A source pond must have a channel from/to it; a drainage pond must have a drain or channel ending on it.
mechanism: Drainage pond: stage_sink sets pond_role='drainage' and draws drain_run(pond_run(...)) whose last point is the pond center (sink.py:pond_run). Source pond: _comb_source_channel starts the hairline at pond_rec (the pond center) with frm pond.

rule: The pond fill must be painted above every course that joins the pond.
mechanism: finish.py:~728 sorts the water entries with the pond fill last (`key=lambda w: bool(w.get('pond_fill'))`) inside the one bed group, so its bedz exceeds every other bed's.

rule: No plot or drain-hem ring edge may cross a field pond's rim (the pond sits inside one plot).
mechanism: _plot_pond shrinks the ellipse until 24 rim points lie inside the host plot and no ring segment enters the core (settlement/_geom/primitives.py:seg_in_ellipse_core, inset 3), else refuses the plot.
sketch: The placer and the test no longer ask the same predicate: the placer allows a ring to enter the outer 3 px band (inset 3), but the test fails any ring with one VERTEX inside the full ellipse and the next outside. Align them: either the placer refuses any ring vertex inside the full ellipse (+ rounding margin), or the test returns to seg_in_ellipse_core.
notes: The shared-predicate docstring in primitives.py says the gate calls seg_in_ellipse_core; the current test does not.

rule: A caption must never be drawn without recording the box of the feature it names (element [6]).
mechanism: Every SEATED caption records its referent: captions.py:_draw_seated_caption computes ref = subject_ref(subject, p) and passes ref=ref to label(); on a hamlet the only caption is the notice board's, queued as 'kosatsuba' and drawn by boards.py:_draw_board_caption -> _draw_seated_caption. Unit tests of the placer: tests/labels/test_placer.py.
sketch: Make the referent mandatory: label()/_record_label (settlement/finish.py) refuse a caption with ref=None unless it is explicitly an area/district caption, so the `text` path cannot emit an anchorless caption.
later_stage_risk: none on a hamlet (stage_labels is last)
notes: The `text` queue path (finish.py:label with ref=None, used by funerary.py, ground.py, trades.py, castle_civic.py, etc.) records no referent; no hamlet stage uses it today (all five pool hamlets caption only the notice board), so the hamlet holds by the absence of such a caller, not by a refusal.

rule: A caption must never stand more than 120 px (box to box) from the feature it names.
mechanism: The candidate set is bounded: placer.py:rings() generates offsets only from PREFERRED_OFFSET_EM to REACH_EM (8 em, labels/standard.py:45), so every point-subject candidate's gap from the subject is at most 8 x size (64 px for the board's 8 pt caption); the frame-exit fallback (placer.py:211) takes the FIRST (ring 0) candidate. Nothing is placed after stage_labels. Tests: tests/labels/test_placer.py.
sketch: Already bounded; to make it explicit, derive REACH_EM from the hug bar (or assert REACH_EM*size < HUG_PX for every caption size used) so a larger caption size cannot outrun it.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: The bound is implicit (8 em * size); it holds for the hamlet's 8 pt board caption with a wide margin (worst ~65 px box gap even on a 45-degree board) but is not stated against 120 px.

rule: A caption on a rotated feature must never be set more than 12 degrees off its subject's angle (mod 180).
mechanism: Every point-subject candidate carries ang = upright(subject.angle) (placer.py:_point_cands, first line), and _draw_seated_caption passes angle=p.angle to label(); the board caption's subject is built with angle=rot (boards.py:_draw_board_caption). Tests: tests/labels/test_placer.py.
sketch: Already by construction for seated captions; the `text` path's label_tilt fold is the only other source of a tilt.
later_stage_risk: none

rule: A caption's drawn block must never come within 2 px of a lane's tread.
sketch: Make a way crossing a refusal, not a cost: in place(), skip any candidate whose ObstacleIndex way-cost is non-zero (WAY_NOTCH is already the test's 2 px) and widen the ring/position set (or move to a leader seat) until a way-clear seat exists; only if none exists anywhere in reach, fail loudly rather than draw it.
later_stage_risk: none (stage_labels is last)
notes: place() scores a way crossing at WEIGHT_WAY=500 (labels/standard.py:53) and takes the cheapest candidate when no zero-cost one exists (placer.py:207-214); since WEIGHT_OBSTACLE=1000 > 500, it will prefer lying across a lane to covering a building. The frame-exit fallback (placer.py:211) returns the first seat with no way test at all.

rule: The notice board must never stand more than 90 px from a way.
mechanism: place_kosatsuba samples seats only at offsets off <= lim = 60 ft/ftpx from a route (siting.py:233, 369); the frame re-seat in hamletgen/frame.py:stage_notice samples only verge seats at tread half-width + KOSATSUBA_VERGE_FT + half depth, and its 'loose' fallback is one of those verge seats (frame.py:301, 356). Tests: tests/hamletgen/test_frame.py, tests/settlement/test_water_ways.py.
sketch: Already constrained; the only failure left is NO board (place_kosatsuba returns None, or the re-seat pops the board and finds no seat), which the test reports as 'posted no board'.
later_stage_risk: none (only stage_labels follows)
notes: The re-seat pops the first board (frame.py ~201) and may place none if every verge fails _fits / fixture_clear_of_water - the rule then holds vacuously but the board is missing.

rule: The notice board must never stand more than 45 degrees off parallel to its nearest way.
mechanism: place_kosatsuba turns the chosen board to nearest_way_bearing(M, x, y) (siting.py:548-550), the shared body with a fixed first-in-manifest tie-break (settlement/_geom/ways.py:111); the frame re-seat refuses any verge whose nearest-way bearing is >15 degrees off the lane it stands on (frame.py:286) and its fallback takes the nearest-way bearing (frame.py:356). Tests: tests/hamletgen/test_frame.py, tests/settlement/test_geom.py.
sketch: Already by construction. Have the gate test call nearest_way_bearing instead of its own scan so the corner tie-break cannot diverge.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: The test re-derives the nearest segment with its own loop (strict <, manifest order over lanes then M['lane']) rather than calling nearest_way_bearing (street_runs order); if the two orders ever differ at an exactly-equidistant corner the test could read the other arm.

rule: A nucleated cluster must never stand with its nearest house more than 700 px from a field, nor any house more than 700 px + two cluster spans away.
mechanism: The front row is seated along the field outline at standoffs out to ~150 px (homesteads/seats.py:front_row, stages.py front-row passes); rescue rounds (attempt >= 4) refuse seats outside in_band (bound = FORM_BOUND * hypot(lat, dep) around the seat center, stages.py in_band / 'if not in_band(...) and attempt >= 4'). The seat itself is on a field margin (cluster.py:seat_cluster).
sketch: Assert field adjacency on the PLACED position: refuse (or re-rank) any homestead seat whose distance to the field outline exceeds the band's depth, in every round including the lattice ranks; the record gives a 6 ft minimum and a ~700 ft tolerance (research/homesteads.html, 'How close does a farmhouse stand to the paddy?').
later_stage_risk: none (houses are not moved after stage_homesteads)
notes: Lattice ranks for attempt < 4 are NOT held to in_band; their depth is bounded only by _row_out + _rank_step*(attempt+1). The _pretest docstring records this as an OPEN DEFECT: 'the fix ... is to assert field adjacency on the PLACED position'. The 700 px bar is a rail, so the risk is small, but nothing measures it.

rule: A map must never declare a cluster_shape its drawn cluster aspect does not fall inside (it must declare the shape honored or record it unhonored).
mechanism: stages.py:604-624 measures the drawn aspect (cluster_aspect over the placed houses) and writes meta.cluster_shape only when it lies inside CLUSTER_DRAWN_ASPECT for the rolled shape (non-round shapes held above round's 2.0 ceiling), else meta.cluster_shape_unhonored; cluster_aspect_drawn is always recorded. Tests: tests/gate/test_generator_contracts.py.
sketch: Already guaranteed as bookkeeping. If the GM wants the SHAPE itself honored (not just declared honestly), the skeleton/front-row seating would have to be shape-aware (consts.py CLUSTER_BAND_ASPECT docstring: the lane skeleton dominates shape).
later_stage_risk: none (houses fixed after stage_homesteads)
notes: The guarantee is that the declaration describes the drawing, not that the rolled shape is drawn; round is honored on ~5 of 21 cohort rolls by the consts.py record.

rule: A settlement must never seat fewer byres than its recorded byre_target.
sketch: Reserve the byre with the homestead: decide the keeper households (BYRE_KEEPER_SHARE, research/homesteads/300) before seating and include the byre arm/shed in the homestead envelope at seat time (the envelope-first placer already carries the kura this way), so a keeper cannot be seated without room for its beast; failing that, walk every household (not only the ranked pool) and widen COURTYARD_REACH before giving up, and raise if the target is still unmet.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: draft_byres loops `while len(out) < target and _pool` (byres.py:287), skipping a boxed-in homestead; when the pool runs out the shortfall ships with byre_target recorded. Placed in stage_appurtenances after the houses and wells, so every courtyard may already be full.

rule: Two farmhouses must never stand closer than FARMHOUSE_EAVE_GAP_FT (8 ft) wall to wall.
mechanism: fit.py:434-469 refuses a house whose true rotated quad comes within FARMHOUSE_EAVE_GAP_FT + 2 ft (poly_gap) of any non-abandoned house; called on every bundle path (fit.py:353, fit.py:605, rolling/place.py:87). Test: tests/settlement/test_rolling.py.
sketch: Already refused at seat time; align the gate's measure with the placer's (rotated quads via poly_gap).
later_stage_risk: none (houses are not moved after placement)
notes: MEASURE MISMATCH: the gate test measures UNROTATED axis-aligned w x h boxes (_edge_gap ignores rot) while the placer measures rotated quads. On a quarter-turned house (Inashiro has one at rot 94.3 with w=45 along x) the test's box runs along the wrong axis, so the test can report a pair the placer correctly admitted.

rule: A threshing yard's house-facing edge must never run more than 0.3 degrees off its house's wall.
mechanism: yards.py:566-571: the yard quad is built with _quad(..., level=_facing) so the house-facing edge's two corners share one inward pull (parallel to the frame), then turned by the house's rot with turn_about. Test: tests/settlement/test_homestead_parts.py (sweeps positions).
sketch: Already by construction.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: The test always reads poly[0]->poly[1] (the N edge); the placer levels the HOUSE-FACING edge, which is N on every bundled homestead but may be E/W/S on the legacy fallback - there the test would read an unlevelled edge.

rule: A farmhouse footprint must never exceed 2.7:1 long to wide.
mechanism: houses.py:658-659 draws a nucleated house's length at px(46)*[0.85,1.35] and depth at px(28)*[0.90,1.10], so the largest possible aspect is 62.1/25.2 = 2.46:1; the dispersed path uses fixed 46x28 / 64x40 scaled uniformly, and the headman 92x56 (rolling/place.py:16). No path can produce > 2.46.
sketch: Already bounded by the size ranges; state the bound as a derived assertion beside the ranges so a change to either factor range cannot silently pass 2.7.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: The test's docstring calls this 'a live guard on a real regression, not a re-measurement of a guarantee', but the size ranges make >2.46 unreachable; only a caller passing an explicit size=(w, h) could exceed it.

rule: A well must never stand more than 95 px (edge gap) from every dwelling.
mechanism: The lattice rungs require the nearest house CENTER within 105-112 px (wells.py:108, 127); the coverage rescue requires a house center within 95 px (wells.py:316), which is strictly inside the 95 px edge gap.
sketch: Use the gate's own measure in every rung: require an EDGE gap <= 95 px to some house (not a center distance of 105-112), and give the last-resort open_seat the same floor.
later_stage_risk: none (houses fixed, wells placed in stage_appurtenances)
notes: A center distance of 112 px to a house whose short half-side is ~13 px leaves an edge gap up to ~99 px > 95, so the lattice can seat a well the test rejects. The last resort (wells.py:335, s.open_seat over the house bbox) has no among-the-dwellings floor at all.

rule: No household may stand more than 760 ft from a well or open water.
mechanism: place_wells scores seats by the worst walk of the needy houses (minimax) and then runs a coverage pass (wells.py ~277-332) that ring-probes a well beside every house still beyond 760 ft of a well and of surface water (surface_water_dist, the gate's own measure).
sketch: Make coverage a hard postcondition: if the ring probe finds no seat for a dry house, fall back to open_seat near THAT house, and if that fails refuse the house seat (feed it to the driver's avoid list, as the reach re-roll does) rather than ship it dry.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: The ring probe can end with spot None and the house simply stays dry; the whole rescue branch is '# pragma: no cover' (never reached on the cohort), so the guarantee is untested in practice.

rule: A bridge deck must never be shorter than the width of the water it crosses.
mechanism: Footplanks: channel_footbridges refuses a deck whose corners do not clear the crossed water (bridges.py:446, _deck_clears_its_water; test tests/settlement/test_city.py). Carried-way decks: the span solves the oblique crossing and seat_deck grows/skews the deck until its corners clear (bridges.py:86-120, 253).
sketch: When seat_deck cannot seat a deck, do not draw the undersized one: re-route/square the way at that crossing (stage_crossings already squares lanes over streams and drawn channels, not field ditches) and re-solve, or refuse the crossing so the way is re-planned.
later_stage_risk: none after stage_crossings (only stage_frame/notice/labels follow)
notes: seat_deck returns (rot, original span, False) when nothing seats (bridges.py:120) and bridges() draws it anyway - its docstring: 'an undersized deck that bridges_span_their_water then fails is better than none'.

rule: A footplank must never be laid off a recorded ditch, nor over the collector/drain rather than a supply ditch.
mechanism: Planks are seated only along a recorded field_ditch's own polyline (_at_arc on d['poly']), so 'stranded' cannot occur; on a POLDER seg_caps sets the drain/feeder/far-toe cap to 0 (hamletgen/water polder_crossing_caps, frame.py:111).
sketch: Refuse role == 'drain' (and 'feeder') in channel_footbridges for every archetype, not only through the polder's seg_caps - the test's grounding is that a plank over the drain crosses the runoff, not the ditch anyone needs.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: On a comb/valley hamlet (the reference) channel_footbridges iterates EVERY field_ditch including the drain; only worth_planking and _plank_reaches_useful_ground decide, and its own comment records a drain getting a plank (cohort seed 5, 996 px drain). The reference roll has none on the drain by circumstance. A plank at a main/drain junction can also measure nearest to the drain.

rule: The drain collector's recorded polyline must never turn 100 degrees or more at any vertex.
sketch: Build the collector so its turns are bounded: drop the last interior vertex when it falls within a few px of the outfall (the `duf` loop at comb.py:695-698 appends hi_u after an arbitrary last u, which makes the 'short hook' drain_heading's docstring describes), or clamp the jitter so every turn stays under the bar; the research grounding is the test's 'a collector turns DOWN the valley'.
later_stage_risk: none (the continuation is a separate channels record)
notes: The test reads only the field_ditches drain record, i.e. the comb collector, not the sink's continuation. comb.py builds it from monotone-u samples with +/-6 px jitter and appends the outfall at hi_u after the loop, so the last segment can be a couple of px long pointing anywhere (sink.py drain_heading docstring: 'A comb's collector ends in a short hook'); a turn of ~90 + ~25 degrees is reachable. sink.py only scores the junction of the CONTINUATION (swings capped at 54 degrees). hill.py builds another drain for the hill archetype.

rule: A main or collector end must never stop on the map in bare ground (it must join water, the crop, the pond or leave the frame).
mechanism: The collector's outfall is always continued: every branch of stage_sink (brook join, off-map route, least-bad route, pond) calls drain_run starting at `out`, the drain's last vertex read back from the manifest (sink.py:drain_outfall), so that end joins a channels record.
sketch: Assert the postcondition where the network is built: after the water stages, check every main/drain end against the same join/crop/frame predicate and extend or clip the end (the comb builder already starts the drain 'inside the field'), refusing the field layout otherwise.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: The drain's HEAD and the mains' ends rely on waterfields/comb.py geometry (the head 'begins AT the westmost delivery ditch's bottom (inside the field)') with no assertion; stage_sink returns without a run when drain_outfall is None.

rule: No more than 35% of the rendered view may be ground no cover, field or built footprint covers.
sketch: Measure the bare fraction over the predicted frame after the scrub scatter (the same 25 px grid) and lay further scrub/grazing parcels into the largest uncovered cells until it is under the bar; the grounding is the GM rule 'margins form a continuous ring'.
later_stage_risk: stage_frame's crop decides the view after the cover is laid
notes: Cover is picture-frame strips outside the cultivated bbox (cover.py ring()) minus the toe side and keep-outs, plus per-map woodland; nothing measures the uncovered share of the view.

rule: The lanes must never fall into more than one network (every lane end within 4 px of the rest).
sketch: Make one-network a postcondition of stage_web: after the last pass, compute _components at the ink tolerance and either route a link (as _join_orphan_ways does) or drop the orphan piece (re-rolling if it strands a house), and give every later lane writer (stage_crossings.square_crossings) a keep-connected check like commit_lane's.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings (round_the_brooks / square_crossings rewrite lane pts after the web)
notes: _join_orphan_ways (sweeps.py:235) tries up to six routed links and its docstring says 'if no route exists the component stays orphaned'; _sweep_debris keeps an isolated fragment when a house it serves has no other way. Passes after the last join (center_lane_ends, cut_the_overruns, cut_past_the_junction, drop_lanes, split_at_crossings, tidy_lane_ends, a_way_onto_the_bund) are not re-checked for connectivity; meet_end_to_end closes some gaps only when may_write allows.

rule: A lane must never turn 140 degrees or more at a vertex, nor make two 50-degree-plus turns within 40 ft.
mechanism: _smooth_web string-pulls every lane and cuts hairpin arms (smooth.py:112ff); may_write (ways/clearance.py:199) refuses a later rewrite that bends worse than before.
sketch: Hold the bend rule at every lane write (commit_lane / may_write refuse a result with a fold or a kink, not only one 'worse than it was'), and square brook crossings with a leg that keeps turns under 50 degrees or re-smooth after stage_crossings.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings: square_crossings (ways/checks.py:350) inserts a 2*half leg across a brook, i.e. two turns of the crossing's obliquity within ~16 ft - a kink when the lane met the brook more than ~50 degrees off square
notes: _smooth_web keeps a hairpin arm longer than _LONG_ARM_FT, or one whose cut would strand a house, and runs only three rounds; many passes run after it (straighten_joints, fold_the_connector_hairpin, tidy/center ends, meet_end_to_end, a_way_onto_the_bund) and may_write is 'no worse than it was', not 'good'.

rule: Two lanes meeting end to end must never double back (>=140 degrees), and no lane may end in a short hook (_HOOK_FT / _HOOK_DEG).
mechanism: straighten_joints repairs hooks (_one_hook via unhooked) and folds (_one_joint via tee) until none CAN be repaired (joints.py:163-226), with the same thresholds the test imports.
sketch: Refuse rather than repair: when neither tee nor unhooked yields a legal rewrite, drop or re-route the lane end; and run the joint/hook rule after the last lane writer (split_at_crossings creates new end-to-end joints after straighten_joints).
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings square_crossings; within stage_web every pass after straighten_joints (split_at_crossings, meet_end_to_end, a_way_onto_the_bund, tidy_lane_ends)
notes: _one_hook/_one_joint return False when no rewrite keeps the web (keeps_the_web) and passes commit_lane; the unrepaired fold or hook ships.

rule: No internal lane end may stop in open ground (end_serves: another way, a house/steading, or the worked ground).
mechanism: _sweep_dangling_ends (sweeps.py:671) pulls back each end with the placer's own predicate end_serves (the test calls the same function) until it serves, empties what cannot be saved.
sketch: Make it the final lane pass and a hard rule: when the pull-back would strand a served house and carry_to_dooryard finds no seat, route the end to the nearest way (as _join_orphan_ways does) instead of restoring the dangling original.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings square_crossings (after the web)
notes: When shortening strands a house, the sweep RESTORES the original pts and tries carry_to_dooryard, which may return None, leaving the dangling end. After the last _sweep_dangling_ends, center_lane_ends, cut_the_overruns, cut_past_the_junction, split_at_crossings, tidy_lane_ends, meet_end_to_end and a_way_onto_the_bund still rewrite ends without re-asking end_serves.

rule: A lane segment longer than 60 px must never run through a house, farm shed or byre.
mechanism: Lanes are laid after every house, shed and byre (driver STAGES order) and routed clear of them: clear_runs(..., tight=walls) and _route(..., walls) use _homestead_polys (ways/fabric.py, houses as rotated rects); _smooth_web's string-pull and may_write (clearance.py:199) refuse a rewrite nearer the fabric.
sketch: Give every lane writer one footprint test (commit_lane currently guards only connectivity), and run it on stage_crossings' square_crossings output too.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings square_crossings rewrites lanes with no footprint test
notes: commit_lane (smooth.py:86) checks only web_pieces; square_crossings and some sweep rewrites do not re-test footprints. The connector is laid in stage_track before the byres, which then refuse corridors (_near_corridor), so the byre side holds.

rule: No farmhouse may be the terminus of more than two free lane ends (within 80 px).
sketch: Count free lane ends per house as the web is laid (_lay_web_lane / _serve_stragglers / the sweeps that end a lane at a dooryard) and, when a third end would terminate at the same house, T it into an existing lane there or drop it; grounding is the 0611 ruling (consts.py: 'two lane ends within 60 ft pointing within 25 degrees are a fork serving one steading').
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings square_crossings
notes: No engine code counts lane ends per house (grep: the rule is named only in comments in touch.py:424 and consts.py:780).

rule: No tree trunk may stand on a lane's tread (within its half-width of the centerline).
mechanism: Every tree writer keeps its trunk off the lane corridors at seat time: village_grove via GroveBlocks(corridors=_corridor_buffers(clump*0.45+4)) (stands.py ~203, 232-247); the commons scatter via _sparse's corridor skip (land/cover.py); woods via _corridor_buffers (shrines_wells/woods.py:204); persimmons via _trunk_blocked(..., lanes half+3 ft) (hamletgen/homesteads/fixtures.py:328); homestead groves are fabric the web routes around (ways/fabric.py).
sketch: Either run the lane rewrite in stage_crossings before the woods, or have square_crossings refuse/redirect a leg onto a recorded trunk (tree_crowns) - the same 'reserve before the later stage draws' rule the scatter uses.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings (after stage_woodland/windbreak/bamboo) moves lanes with square_crossings and never looks at tree_crowns

rule: No shipped hamlet's lanes may form more than one network at the 4 ft ink tolerance (_TOUCH_GAP).
sketch: Same as the one-network rule: a stage_web postcondition at _TOUCH_GAP (not _LANE_JOIN_FT), with a link-or-drop repair and a keep-connected check on every later lane writer.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings square_crossings
notes: Reads the committed pool manifests (static data). _join_orphan_ways joins at _LANE_JOIN_FT, a looser reach than the 4 ft ink tolerance; meet_end_to_end and the final _touch_junctions close ink gaps only where may_write/their own legality allow.

rule: No shipped hamlet may carry an internal lane end that reaches nothing (end_serves).
mechanism: As for the reference roll: _sweep_dangling_ends applies end_serves, the same predicate the test calls.
sketch: As for the reference roll: make the end rule the last lane pass and route rather than restore when a pull-back would strand a house.
later_stage_risk: stage_crossings square_crossings
notes: Reads the committed pool manifests; same escape (restore + carry_to_dooryard None) and same post-sweep passes as the reference-roll test.

rule: No two features whose overlap classes forbid it may overlap (matrix_violations) on the comb reference hamlet.
mechanism: Each placer refuses overlaps with what it tests (e.g. _fits against placed boxes, block_polys and corridors; the bundle placer's _bundle_fits; bridges() one-deck-per-place; channel_footbridges' house/dry-plot/deck refusals).
sketch: Have the placers consult the taxonomy they are judged by: index the classified extents once (matrix_extents) and make _fits and every scatter/linear writer refuse a seat that matrix_policy forbids against what is already drawn.
later_stage_risk: any later stage drawing over ground an earlier stage claimed without that pair in its own keep-out list (the test docstring's own caveat)
notes: matrix_policy/matrix_violations (overlap/matrix.py) are called by NO placer - only by this test - so the taxonomy is an audit, not a constraint; coverage of pairs depends on each placer's hand-kept keep-outs.

rule: No two features whose overlap classes forbid it may overlap on the polder (Kuwabata) hamlet.
mechanism: As for the comb hamlet: per-placer keep-outs (plus pond_fixture_fits for sties, farm_fixtures.py:170).
sketch: As for the comb hamlet: placers consult matrix_policy through one indexed extent set.
later_stage_risk: as for the comb hamlet
notes: The polder adds dikes, ring canal, fishponds and sties whose pairs are only as covered as each placer's own list; no placer reads the matrix.

rule: Ground cover (commons, marshes) must never be drawn over a swept clearing or any feature its class may not overlap.
mechanism: Stage order reserves the known clearings first: stage_burial runs before the scatter, and farmstead_fixtures (the household shrines) runs inside stage_hinterland before the commons call; the scatter skips every clearing in self.clearings (land/cover.py:_clear_ground).
sketch: Refuse a clearing registered after a scatter it intersects (or re-sweep the cover under it), i.e. move every clearing-reserving placer before stage_hinterland as a checked invariant using the recorded seq ordinal.
later_stage_risk: a clearing registered after the scatter (the marsh is laid before farmstead_fixtures in stage_hinterland)
notes: 'clearings' is in _MX_NOT_GEOMETRY (overlap/taxonomy.py:572), so matrix_violations never reports a clearings pair: the test as written only sees commons/marshes vs forbidden classes, not the ordering it is named for. The seq ordinal recorded for this rule is read by nothing.

rule: No pig sty may stand within SLUICE_CLEAR_FT (6 ft) of a pond sluice stub.
mechanism: pond_fixture_fits refuses any seat whose rotated shed footprint is within px(SLUICE_CLEAR_FT) of any dikepond_sluices segment (poly_seg_dist, zero on overlap) (farm_fixtures.py:182-190); stage_pond_stock takes only seats that pass it (pondstock.py). Tests: tests/settlement/test_farm_fixtures.py.
sketch: Already refused at seat time.
later_stage_risk: none (sluices are laid by the water stages before stage_pond_stock)

rule: A pig sty must never stand further from the house cluster's centroid than its pond parcel's center.
mechanism: stage_pond_stock accepts a bank seat only if math.dist(seat, hc) <= reach, reach = the parcel centroid's distance to hc (pondstock.py, the `next(...)` over _bank_seats); hc is the mean of M['houses'], which no later stage changes.
sketch: Already bounded at seat time.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: Research: specs/233-pigsty-clear-of-the-sluice/research.md R7.

rule: A woodland commons parcel must never record fewer than 5 crowns (or none).
sketch: After seating a woodland's crowns, refuse the parcel (drop it and try the next scanned patch) when fewer than the stocking floor seated; or have open_ground_patches pre-test crown seats so a parcel is only offered where the floor can be met.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: commons(role='woodland') tries _wd_target*6 random seats filtered by _sparse and the crown index (cover.py ~255-280) and records whatever count results (`crowns: _wd_crowns`); there is no floor. The reference roll has lost its woodland entirely at times, so the test falls back to a pool manifest.

rule: A woodland commons parcel must never stand more than half in marsh.
mechanism: open_ground_patches refuses a candidate square if any of its 3x3 sample points (center, edge midpoints, corners) falls in a recorded marsh (parcels.py:243-244, _wet); the marsh is laid first in stage_hinterland (s.hinterland(commons=False)) and the pond fringe/waterward marshes earlier.
sketch: Already refused at scan time; sample the drawn ring at the gate's 5x5 if the two measures should agree exactly.
later_stage_risk: none (no marsh is laid after stage_hinterland)
notes: The placer's 3x3 probe of the square is not the gate's 5x5 grid over the drawn ring's bbox, but a parcel with no probe point in marsh cannot be >50% marsh except for a marsh finger threading between probes.

rule: A woodland commons parcel's box must never fall less than 70% inside the rendered view.
mechanism: parcel_bbox_ok (parcels.py:52-75) refuses a seat whose ROTATED parcel bbox keeps less than WOODLAND_BBOX_FLOOR (0.72) inside the predicted kept frame (content_box).
sketch: Seat the woodland against the FINAL view, or re-test after stage_frame and drop/move a parcel that fell under the floor.
later_stage_risk: stage_frame's crop_to_content computes the real view after the scan; parity holds only while every frame-setting feature is placed before stage_hinterland
notes: The parcels.py note asserts the predicted box equals the final meta.view 'because everything that sets the frame is placed before the woodland scan runs' - an ordering fact, not a check.

rule: A recorded village grove must never hold fewer than 1.5 clumps per 100k sq px of its recorded w x h.
sketch: Record the grove's extent as the drawn clumps' extent (not the requested footprint), or refuse/re-seat a grove whose clump density falls below the floor after seating.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: village_grove records a grove 'IF any clump is drawn' (stands.py docstring) with the bbox of the requested poly; a footprint mostly refused by houses/crops/sun corridors records a large outline with a few clumps.

rule: No copse clump may stand inside a windbreak/water-mouth clump's canopy radius.
mechanism: The copse is drawn after the belt (hinterland/stages.py:233 windbreak, :304 copse) and village_grove refuses any clump within r + 0.9*clump of an already-recorded village_groves clump (occ_grove, stands.py:201-202, passed as circles/displacers to GroveBlocks).
sketch: Already refused at seat time.
later_stage_risk: none
notes: No direct unit test of occ_grove found (grep tests for occ_grove: none).

rule: No village grove clump may stand within 4 px of a channel or stream centerline.
mechanism: GroveBlocks(water=[(line, half_width + cr)]) over every stream and channel (stands.py ~227-240) refuses a clump center nearer than the water's half-width plus the clump radius, which exceeds 4 px; the water is all laid before the woods.
sketch: Already refused at seat time.
later_stage_risk: none (no watercourse is added after stage_windbreak)

rule: The CLI parses its arguments into the reference spec and reports the map it gets back.
notes: CLI wiring; generate() is monkeypatched to serve the cached roll.

rule: roll_pool's process fan-out returns the same specs in the same order as the serial path.
notes: Stub producer; nothing is placed.

rule: A pinned knob is honored identically on every regen, and an out-of-space or geography-violating pin raises.
notes: Knob/determinism bookkeeping on roll_village.

rule: A shipped scripted map must never paint a field channel under a later paddy plot, and its typical paddy cell must never leave the 0.030-0.072 acre band (plus: the gen runs within its CPU budget).
owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/fields/comb.py:draw_comb_field (channel z-order) and the comb carve's plot_across calibration in l7r/diagram/hamletgen/water/fit.py:fit_field (cell size)
